config.goal: Port llm.c's GPT-2 test, test_gpt2_fp32.cu, to SYCL 2020 as test_gpt2_fp32.cpp, with zero dpct helpers. Like the CUDA test it starts with `#define TESTING` and `#include "train_gpt2_fp32.cpp"`: train_gpt2_fp32.cpp in the work dir is your own SYCL port of llm.c's trainer, already proven against llm.c (its training losses match llm.c's own trainer). Change train_gpt2_fp32.cpp only to wrap its main in `#ifndef TESTING` ... `#endif`, as train_gpt2_fp32.cu does; leave the rest of it as it is. Port the test's main (device setup, loading gpt2_124M_debug_state.bin, the logits, loss and gradient comparisons and the 10 training steps) using the trainer's functions, with the same printout ('step %d: loss %f ...', 'overall okay: %d'). Compile with sources [test_gpt2_fp32.cpp]. A hidden check runs your test and requires 'overall okay: 1' and 10 step losses that match PyTorch's within 1e-2 (llm.c's test tolerance). Success requires compile, verify and a zero-helper scan_helpers of the whole work directory (path '.') on the same sources; delete migrate's output (delete_file) once your port is done. What the test needs from train_gpt2_fp32.cpp: the device queue is the global `static sycl::queue *g_q` (the trainer's main sets it: `sycl::queue q{ sycl::property::queue::in_order{} }; g_q = &q;`; `qq()` returns it); the model's tensors are device USM (sycl::malloc_device), so copy with qq().memcpy(dst, src, bytes).wait(); the functions are gpt2_build_from_checkpoint(GPT2*, path), gpt2_forward(GPT2*, int* inputs, int* targets, B, T), gpt2_zero_grad(GPT2*), gpt2_backward(GPT2*), gpt2_update(GPT2*, lr, beta1, beta2, eps, weight_decay, t) and gpt2_free(GPT2*); the fields are model.acts.output, model.grads.<tensor>, model.grads_memory, model.mean_loss, model.config.*, model.param_sizes and model.num_parameters. main is the last function in train_gpt2_fp32.cpp: add the guard with two small edit_file calls (put `#ifndef TESTING` before the `int main(int argc, char *argv[]) {` line, and `#endif` after main's closing brace at the end of the file), not by rewriting the file. You do not need to read the whole trainer: write test_gpt2_fp32.cpp within your first few turns, then compile and verify, and fix what the compiler and verify report.

suggestions.include: Remove #include <dpct/...> once no dpct:: symbols remain.
suggestions.device_queue_management: Own an explicit sycl::queue (e.g. created once in main and passed down) instead of dpct::get_current_device()/in_order_queue(); query device info with q.get_device().get_info<sycl::info::device::...>().
suggestions.macro: Remove DPCT_* macros (e.g. DPCT_CHECK_ERROR, DPCT_PROFILING_ENABLED) and use plain SYCL.
suggestions.library_wrappers: Call the library directly instead of dpct::blas/fft/rng wrappers: oneMath (oneapi::math::blas::column_major::gemm(q, ...), vendor-portable) or oneMKL / oneDNN / oneCCL. Replace a dpct::blas::descriptor handle with the sycl::queue itself.
suggestions.other: Unclassified dpct:: helper: inspect and replace with the SYCL 2020 equivalent.
suggestions.error_handling: SYCL reports errors with exceptions: delete dpct::err0/DPCT_CHECK_ERROR plumbing and wrap the work in try { ... } catch (const sycl::exception&) plus an async_handler on the queue.
suggestions.types_launch: Use sycl::range<N>/sycl::nd_range<N> directly instead of dpct::dim3 and launch kernels with q.parallel_for.
suggestions.math_intrinsics: Use sycl:: math builtins (sycl::min, sycl::max, sycl::pow, sycl::clamp, sycl::bit_cast) or std:: equivalents in host code.
suggestions.memory_management: Use sycl::malloc_device/malloc_shared + q.memcpy/q.memset + sycl::free(ptr, q). Replace dpct::constant_memory/global_memory with a plain USM allocation or a kernel argument.
